newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's BNI Jan-June bad loans down--report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's BNI Jan-June bad loans down--report.

text.p: State-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), which plans to float shares in November, said bad loans in the first six months of 1996 were lower than in the previous six-month period, the Jakarta Post reported on Wednesday.

BNI's bad loans from January to June 1996 totalled 1.18 trillion rupiah against 1.39 trillion rupiah at the end of last year, the newspaper quoted commercial director Hendrick Willem Tehabijuluw as saying.
Hendrick said that of the total, problem loans totalled 544 billion rupiah, doubtful loans 340 billion rupiah and bad debt 297 billion rupiah.
"What is certain is that we will be able to manage our bad loans. Our bad loans represent 5.7 percent of total credits which is better than the banking industry average," Hendrick said.
He made the comments at a presentation to prospective shareholders in the central Java city of Semarang as part of the BNI roadshow to promote its initial public offering in November.
The bank plans to list a 25 percent-stake, or one billion shares, on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges.
